name: Neru Fragment
summary: Unearthed from disturbed earth, the Neru Fragment carries part of the Goaz Stone's ancient Titan script. The relic was discovered at Whelgar's Excavation in the Wetlands, and its words tell of Azeroth's primeval history.

sections.title: Piece of the Goaz Stone
sections.body: Prospector Whelgar led the dwarven expedition that discovered the Goaz Stone. The relic broke into four pieces: Ados, Modr, Golm, and Neru. Raptors overran the dig, halting the work, and the Neru Fragment remained beneath loose soil among the aggressive beasts. Once recovered, it can join the other pieces and restore the tablet. Its surviving words speak of a divine plan and a doomed prophecy, giving dwarven scholars a record to decipher.

sections.title: Reading the Restored Tablet
sections.body: With all four fragments gathered, Prospector Whelgar restores the Goaz Stone and continues translating its Titan script. The newly legible words tell of Old Gods chained beneath the land.

faq.answer: The Neru Fragment is an ancient stone piece broken from the Goaz Stone, a larger relic. The dwarven expedition uncovered it in the Wetlands before raptors overran the dig.
The Neru Fragment lies scattered in Whelgar's Excavation, east of Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. It is typically buried under loose soil or hidden among abandoned artifacts.

faq.q: What happens when all four fragments are gathered?
aliases: what does the goaz stone say
faq.answer: After all four fragments are gathered, Prospector Whelgar pieces the Goaz Stone back together and continues translating its Titan script, pursuing the mystery hinted at by the surviving text.

angles.text: For the Explorer's League, recovering tablet pieces like the Neru Fragment is vital to unearthing Titan secrets and piecing together the origins of dwarven kind.
